1: "Return to me, and I will return to you." Zechariah sees horsemen patrolling the earth and four horns that scattered Judah.
2: A man goes to measure Jerusalem. It will overflow its walls, and God will be a wall of fire around it.
"Many nations shall join themselves to the Lord."
3: The high priest Joshua stands in filthy clothes with Satan accusing him. God rebukes Satan and has Joshua clothed in clean robes.
God removes guilt and silences the accuser.
4: A golden lampstand and two olive trees. "Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit."
God's work is done by God's Spirit.
5: A huge scroll flies out against thieves and liars. Wickedness is carried off in a basket to Babylon.
Sin is removed from the land.
6: Chariots go out to the four winds. A crown is set on the high priest Joshua, a sign of "the Branch" who will build the Lord's Temple.
Priest and king united point to Christ.
7: Asked about fast days, God answers: show kindness and mercy, and do not oppress the widow or the poor.
8: Old people will sit in the streets and children play there. Ten men from the nations will take hold of one Jew, saying, "God is with you."
9: "Rejoice, daughter of Zion! Your king comes to you, humble and riding on a donkey."
10: The people wander like sheep without a shepherd. God will bring them home.
11: The prophet acts as shepherd of a doomed flock and is paid thirty pieces of silver, which he throws into the Temple.
Matthew sees this fulfilled in Judas.
12: God pours out a spirit of grace and prayer. "They shall look on him whom they have pierced, and mourn."
John quotes this at the crucifixion.
13: A fountain is opened to cleanse from sin. "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered."
Jesus quotes this on the night of his arrest.
14: The nations attack Jerusalem, the Lord fights for it, and living waters flow from the city.
"The Lord will be king over all the earth."
